Keeping this in one place means the shared household id and the household-membership 30 * lookup can never drift apart: two owners belong to the same household exactly when the 31 * identity fields this resolver keys on (their normalized last name and postcode) agree, and 32 * for that household they derive an identical id. 33 * 34 *

The household id is deterministic: the first twelve hex characters of the SHA-256 digest 35 * of the normalized last name and the postcode joined by '|'. Owners that share a normalized 36 * last name and postcode therefore derive the same id automatically, without any explicit 37 * link. 38 */ 39 @Component 40 public class HouseholdResolver { 41 42 private final ClinicService clinicService; 43 44 public HouseholdResolver(ClinicService clinicService) { 45 this.clinicService = clinicService; 46 } 47 48 /** 49 * The stable, shared household identifier for {@code owner}: the first twelve hex 50 * characters of {@code SHA-256(normalizedLastName + '|' + postcode)}. Owners in the same 51 * household (same normalized last name and postcode) derive an identical id. 52 * 53 * @param owner the owner whose household id is derived 54 * @return the deterministic household id 55 */ 56 public String householdId(Owner owner) { 57 String postcode = owner.getPostcode() == null ? "" : owner.getPostcode(); 58 String key = IdentityUtils.normalizeIdentity(owner.getLastName()) + "|" + postcode; 59 return HashUtils.sha256HexPrefix(key, 12); 60 } 61 62 /** 63 * Whether an existing owner already belongs to {@code owner}'s household, i.e. shares its 64 * computed household id (same normalized last name and postcode). Such a second owner is a 65 * household duplicate unless it deliberately declares {@code sharesHousehold}. 66 * 67 * @param owner the owner about to be created 68 * @return {@code true} if an already-registered owner shares this owner's household 69 */ 70 public boolean householdExists(Owner owner) { 71 String householdId = householdId(owner); 72 return this.clinicService.findAllOwners().stream() 73 .filter(existing -> !existing.isDeleted()) 74 .anyMatch(existing -> householdId.equals(householdId(existing))); 75 } 76 } 77

content.text: The refactor compiles, the Spring context wires the new `OwnerRegistrar` bean, and behavior is unchanged — the second create still returns 409, identical to the pre-refactor baseline. The one failing test (`coreIdempotentRepeat`) is the acceptance test for the not-yet-implemented idempotency change itself, so it stays red exactly as it was before I started. Let me confirm the baseline was already red on that same test (it was — same 200-vs-409 failure), and view the final controller.

The restructuring is complete. Here's what I did and why.

## What I found

The only test in the suite, `AcceptanceTest.coreIdempotentRepeat`, is the acceptance test for the *upcoming* idempotency change — and it was already red at baseline (expects `200`, gets `409` because a repeated create is a duplicate). Since I was told not to implement that change, this test necessarily stays red; making it green would mean building the feature.

## The restructuring

The two flagged symbols pointed at one root cause: `addOwner` inlined the entire ~100-line owner-creation pipeline, and the constructor carried 8 collaborators — four of which (`TelephoneNormalizer`, `AddressNormalizer`, `CityRegionResolver`, `HouseholdResolver`) existed purely to serve that pipeline. The idempotency change would have added a *ninth* dependency and more branching inside an already-overloaded method.

This codebase already has a clear, recently-established idiom: single-concern `@Component` collaborators in the `rest.controller` package (`HouseholdResolver`, `CityRegionResolver`, `TelephoneNormalizer`, `AddressNormalizer`), each documented as "the single place that owns concern X." I followed that idiom exactly:

- **New `OwnerRegistrar` `@Component`** — owns the owner-creation concern end to end. It holds the create pipeline (`register`), the create-specific collaborators, and all the create-only private helpers (`normalizedAddress`, `isDuplicateOwner`, `possibleDuplicateOf`, `customerCode`, `namesakeCount`, `toBusinessDay`, `membershipNumber`) plus the create-only constants and the `AUDIT` logger — moved **verbatim** to preserve behavior.
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1`** — constructor drops from 8 params to 5 (leaving room for the coming idempotency store), and `addOwner` becomes a one-line delegation to `ownerRegistrar.register(...)`.

This gives the change a clean seam: `register(...)` returns the create outcome as a `ResponseEntity`, so idempotency handling (read the header, short-circuit to the stored owner with `200`, or record the key after a successful create) lands entirely in the controller's HTTP boundary without touching the pipeline.

## Verification

The project compiles, the Spring context wires the new bean, and behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged: the repeated create still returns `409`, identical to the pre-refactor baseline. No previously-passing test was broken. The sole failing test remains `coreIdempotentRepeat`, which is the not-yet-implemented feature's own acceptance test — red before my work and red after, by design.
